html:
The Nom Sus are one of the bands of the Wintu, a people of the upper Sacramento River valley and the mountains west of it in Northern California. The name is usually read as "west people", for bands living on the western side of the valley.

The Wintu fished salmon, gathered acorns and hunted. Their bands include the Winnimem on the McCloud River and the Nom Ti Pom further up. During the Gold Rush miners and settlers killed and displaced many Wintu. The Shasta Dam later flooded villages and burial grounds of the region.
